## Current research direction {#current-direction}

My current research examines how knowledge, values, and emerging AI practices move through research and learning communities. I am especially interested in how people learn, collaborate, trust, and make responsible decisions with emerging technologies.

## Emerging PhD research {#emerging-phd-research}

My PhD research is still taking shape. I am interested in extending my earlier interview and network research to examine how researchers' values and experiences shape AI use, how emerging practices spread through research communities, and how those patterns affect interdisciplinary collaboration. The unpublished AIROE interviews may provide a foundation for expanding this work while I continue developing questions about research integrity, institutional change, and responsible decision-making with AI.

Several collaborations have shaped this direction. [Trace the progression through my human-centered AI collaborations](human-centered-ai-collaborations.qmd), from AIROE and the AI Institute to the developing Idaho Institute for Human-Centered AI.

## Master’s thesis foundation {#masters-thesis}

My master’s thesis used social network analysis to examine interdisciplinary collaboration in Boise State’s Grand Challenges initiative. This project helped shape my current interest in knowledge networks, collaboration structures, and the conditions that support or limit interdisciplinary research.

[Read my master’s thesis](https://doi.org/10.18122/td.2143.boisestate){target="_blank"}.
